# HD 209458 b: solar-minimum spectrum normalized as Salz et al. (2016)
# columns: wavelength [A]  flux at the planet [erg cm^-2 s^-1 A^-1]
# reference: Salz et al. (2016), A&A 586, A75 (2016A&A...586A..75S),
#            section 2.2, four spectral regions: a 2 MK CHIANTI plasma model
#            for 0-100 A normalized to L_X, a Gaussian Lya normalized to
#            L_Lya, an inactive solar EUV shape over 100-912 A normalized
#            to L_EUV, and a photospheric blackbody longward of a
#            connection point between 1500 and 4000 A.
# shape:     Solar Irradiance Reference Spectrum of the 2008 Whole
#            Heliosphere Interval (Woods et al. 2009, GRL 36, L01101),
#            column 'March 30 - April 4 (6-day average)', solar minimum,
#            for every region (its X-rays stand in for the CHIANTI model).
# geometry:  irradiance at 1 au x (1 au / a)^2 = 448.295221 with a = 0.04723 AU
#            (header of the CDS table J/A+A/586/A75/hd209458.dat).
# step 1:    lambda < 100 A x 3.751906e-01 so that F(5-100 A) at the planet is
#            L_X / (4 pi a^2) = 4.0041e+01 erg cm^-2 s^-1 with log L_X = 26.40
#            (Salz Table 3, an upper limit, 0.124-2.48 keV).
# step 2:    Lya window 1208.0-1226.0 A, the line above its local continuum
#            (medians of 1195-1205 and 1226-1237 A) x 3.365177e+00 so that the line
#            flux is 9.3865e+03 erg cm^-2 s^-1 with log L_Lya = 28.77 (Salz
#            Table 3). Salz's 9.4 A Gaussian is not reproduced: they state
#            it is set by their solver's 6.1 A resolution, not by the star.
# step 3:    100-911.6 A x 9.012718e-01 so that F(100-912 A) at the planet is
#            L_EUV / (4 pi a^2) = 1.1028e+03 erg cm^-2 s^-1 with
#            log L_EUV = 27.84 (Salz Table 3, an upper limit, 100-912 A).
# step 4:    longward of 911.6 A no renormalization, only (1 au / a)^2: the
#            Sun's surface flux in place of Salz's 6065 K blackbody, whose
#            connection point they do not state.
# joins:     f(above)/f(below) = 3.6551 at 100 A and 1.1064 at 911.6 A, measured.
# check:     F(1-912 A) = 1.1436e+03, log = 3.0583, against Salz's
#            log F_XUV = 3.06 (<912 A at the planet).
# negatives: 0 source rows below zero set to 0
# coverage:  0.500000 to 4999.5000 A, 5000 rows, strictly increasing.
# built by inputdata/sed/build/build_hd209458b_solar_salz.py
